conbody.p: Purpose of Home Device Manager. Home Device Manager allows broadband providers to remotely manage CPE (customer premises equipment), such as residential gateways, DSL and cable modems, femtocell access points, IP set-top boxes, and VoIP terminal adapters. Allowing for large-scale remote management of a multi-vendor CPE network, Home Device Manager offers a standardized CPE integration layer that enables providers to manage CPE that support either the Broadband Forum's TR-069 protocol or other protocols such as Telnet.

Home Device Manager standard and optional features: Home Device Manager includes the Proactive Management Engine that allows policy-based automation of device configuration and management. The Northbound Interface (NBI) also provides a standardized web services interface for existing OSS infrastructure and integration with other Motive™ products such as Service Management Platform (SMP) and Home Care. In addition, the Traffic Regulation Module (TRM) is an optional module that uses input throttling to regulate massive amounts of traffic data collected from CPEs, the Intelligent Workflow Engine (IWE) extends HDM's proactive management functionalities by allowing service providers to customize service management workflows, and the Generic TR-069 Proxy offers the capability to communicate and manage non-TR-069 devices. As a key benefit to providers, Home Device Manager enables single as well as large-scale bulk device configuration, troubleshooting, firmware upgrades, event management, alarm management, and user management.
